summary: A square wooden tower of 1872 at Cap-de-Caissie, built to guide steamers to the railway port of Shediac on the Northumberland Strait.

Caissie Point Light commenced operation on August 30th, 1872, exhibiting a flashing white light produced by two banks of lamps each of which was backed by an eighteen-inch reflector.
The light completed a revolution every three minutes, thus producing a white flash every ninety seconds.
Masters of steamers and other vessels trading to and from the railway terminus at Shediac highly praised the new light.

notes_for_editor: Thin station. Record says deactivated 2021; no source found confirming (register says current function navigational aid; Lighthouse Friends says active). Lighthouse Friends internally inconsistent on LeBlanc end (1901 text vs 1909 list); 1903/1904 tables still list him (matched by column position in OCR). Alfred Gallant 1914 date and the 1915 Cassie point reflector work were matched by column/row position in OCR tables. 1904 'May 4, 1872' also positional. Keeper roster from Lighthouse Friends only; no archive roster for Canada. Story text on 1871 Harding report is second-hand via Lighthouse Friends. Verifier 2026-10-27: read page images for 1900 pp.53-54 (Cassie point is in the hand fog horn list that starts on p.53), 1903 (printed p.215) and 1904 (printed p.159) keeper rows, 1915 p.44 and p.66 (Gallant row aligned to Cassie point); all confirmed. 1991 date added from Heritage Guide page for entry 10989.
